limitations: Removal is not the same as failure: it includes mergers, asset transfers, dissolution and removal for non-filing, so the label is a register-exit event rather than an insolvency or effectiveness measure.

The bulk extract is a current-vintage snapshot: classification, area, activities and governing-document fields carry no as-of-registration timestamp, so they are treated as registration-time descriptors but may reflect later edits; this does not establish historical operational availability.
Charities removed after the five-year anniversary are coded negative, so late exits are right-censored by design.
The register covers England and Wales only; Scotland (OSCR) and Northern Ireland (CCNI) are separate regulators and are excluded.
The register includes personal data (trustee names, contact details) that the OGL does not cover; the derived release must exclude those fields and use organisation-level attributes only.
Legal-form conversions after registration (for example to a CIO) can change the current charity_type, creating a small vintage mismatch with the decision instant.
The removal date is not the date the charity ceased to exist or ceased to operate, so the label should not be read as an organisational death date.
Removal is a register-exit event, not insolvency, failure or organisational death; it includes mergers, asset transfers, dissolution and removal for non-filing.

The bulk extract is a current-vintage snapshot; classification, area, governing-document and objects fields carry no as-of-registration timestamp, so they are assumed registration-time descriptors and may reflect later edits.
Charities removed after the fifth anniversary are coded negative, so late exits are right-censored by design.
England and Wales only; Scotland and Northern Ireland are separate regulators.
Personal data in the register is excluded; only organisation-level attributes are shipped.
Legal-form conversions after registration can create a vintage mismatch.
date_of_removal is not the date the charity ceased to exist or ceased to operate.

The shipped date_of_registration is the prediction-time anchor and part of the cohort definition, not an answer source; the answer sources (date_of_removal and charity_registration_status) are never shipped.

Actual column names and status spellings were not re-read during this write-only construction; the builder resolves documented and plausible aliases and raises with observed headers and archive member if a field or join is unresolved.
No persistence reference is available because each organisation appears once in the cohort.
No uncertainty interval; observed differences do not establish universal headroom

paragraphs: Will a charity newly entered on the Register of Charities for England and Wales be removed from the register within five years of its registration date?

Population: Main charities only, where linked_charity_number equals 0, with date_of_registration from 2015-01-01 through 2018-12-31 inclusive, whose charity_registration_status normalises to registered or removed, excluding rows where date_of_removal precedes date_of_registration. One row per organisation_number; linked and subsidiary charities are excluded.

Target: y = 1 if date_of_removal is non-null and is on or before the fifth anniversary of date_of_registration; y = 0 if there is no removal on or before that anniversary, including charities still registered or removed later.

Prediction time: date_of_registration, the day the charity is entered on the register. Only attributes present in the current daily extract are treated as registration-time descriptors; classification, area, governing-document and objects fields are not time-stamped, so their as-of-registration availability is assumed rather than verified.

Splits: Chronological by date_of_registration: train = registrations from 2015-01-01 through 2016-12-31; eval = 2017-01-01 through 2017-12-31; holdout = 2018-01-01 through 2018-12-31. No embargo is applied because every input is fixed at the row's own registration date and the label is the row's own forward five-year exit; there are no lagged, rolling or cross-row features. All five-year outcome windows close by 2023-12-31, well before the extract date.

Outcome horizon: Five years (to the registration-date anniversary) after date_of_registration; the removal date is observed through the extract date, which is at least seven years later for every eligible cohort.

Inputs: charity_type: Legal or administrative type displayed on the register, such as charitable company, CIO, trust or unincorporated association.; charity_is_cio: Whether the charity is a Charitable Incorporated Organisation, normalised to a binary flag with empty meaning unknown.; has_company_registration: Whether the charity has a Companies House registration number in the current extract.; classification_what: Sorted semicolon-separated register classification codes for the What category, aggregated per organisation. Missing means no linked What row, not a none category.; classification_who: Sorted semicolon-separated register classification codes for the Who category, aggregated per organisation. Missing means no linked Who row, not a none category.; area_of_operation_scope: Sorted semicolon-separated distinct area-of-operation descriptions aggregated per organisation. This is a scope profile rather than a single ranked scope because the current extract does not evidence a documented geographic hierarchy. Missing is not zero.; governing_document_description: Short description of the governing-document type from the linked governing-document table, whitespace-normalised.; objects_text: Text of the charitable objects from the linked governing-document table, whitespace-normalised for a bag-of-words or hashed representation.
